title: Variational Inference
interviewAnswer: Variational inference converts difficult posterior inference into optimization: choose a tractable q(z) and optimize it to approximate the true posterior, commonly by maximizing the ELBO.
why: VI is central to VAEs and scalable Bayesian models.
intuition: Instead of sampling indefinitely from a hard posterior, fit a simpler distribution that approximates it.
deepDive: The ELBO contains an expected data-fit term minus KL(q||prior) and lower-bounds log evidence. The approximation family itself can limit posterior quality.
production: VI can be fast but may underestimate uncertainty; validate posterior predictive behavior.
workedExample: A VAE encoder outputs q(z|x) parameters and trains via an ELBO rather than computing p(z|x) exactly.
